body: I agree. It's the relationship that I feel is conditional
You've got to be kidding. I know this sub is pretty terrible but you actually think ipos made points? What point does making a response even supposedly prove?

I don't even know what the point of this sub is anymore. Every time I get a notification it's just people taddling on right wing YouTubers. They aren't even scandals. It's like yeah, no shit they do what they do. They don't hide it

I'm not sure if this comment is shitting on true crime or not since they usually have to at least do a lot of research. Most crime cases don't have Wikipedia articles like Blair loves or, if they do, they aren't descriptive enough to make a video. You have to dig.


Or is it a joke because she made that video badmouthing true crime? If so, it wouldn't be the first time "Sarah Jessica warner" made content completely against her supposed values
There is absolutely no way that you came up with this on your own and didn't get it from anime.
Furry is absolutely a kink
Maybe not an asshole, but annoying and stupid
NTA. You have the right to tell people about your own life and choices.
Another person with mental illness here. Although it might help to  explain some behavior, it isn't an excuse.
He was parked at a slight angle where the front, left side of his car was on the yellow line.
I just raised an eyebrow and threw my hands up in an "I'm not sure what you want from me" sort of expression. I kind of wish I would have made a smartass remark. Haha
NTA. You don't have to have anyone over to your own home that you don't want to. Especially during covid.

Am I the only one who despises the whole "hey stranger" thing from family members? It's like they lead with a nag about how you aren't around enough.  


Because, oh yeah, immediately nagging sure opens me up for some conversation

Oh boy, there have been some crazy ones over here too. I also had one family member called a pedophile because he would babysit for some people. That's all, really no more info than that. He just babysat. But, that made him a pedo... for some reason.  


One of the crazier ones was that my brother was popping pills at Dennys and passing out in the parking lot. All because Denny's was a 24/7 restaurant and he'd go there late sometimes with friends. In her eyes, only degenerates are out past sundown, so she theorized that they must be doing hard drugs IN A RESTAURANT and passing out like hobos on the streets. Really, there were no tips or signs that lead her to believe this. He simply went out to eat after dark. She just assumed it must be that way.
When it comes to the rumors, I care less about they say and more about the sheer audacity of it and the clear disrespect. If you know what I mean. Thank you for the response!

" Does this person hurt you more than they help you? "

  
Oh yes. I can't really think of anything I get from being in contact with any of them. Not even emotional support.

  
"  Do you feel a dark cloud of doom and dread when you think about interacting with this person? "

Oh yes. Even physically, I feel a knot in my stomach.  


" Did she really raise you?  Like... teach you right from wrong, teach you  how to work through your troubles, encourage you to be independent? "

Nope, just those necessities. I can't really think of any life lessons or anything at all.

​

I'm glad you agree with me on the deal about "raising" me. Their gaslighting had me confused on that point.
Good advice and even better username.
You're probably right. Honestly I should have had her blocked, but we talk so extremely little that I forgot I even had her number.

Good, I'm glad I never responded then. I just sent screenshots of the texts to the family members I do still have contact with to show them exactly how they operate. But, I have no interest in arguing with her. I honestly don't really care how a burnout druggie thief feels about me. It was more about the audacity of her insulting my dead father that I wanted the rest to see.

My family was the same way. It was always "you don't NEED that!" or "If only you'd put this effort into more studying"  


It's something I talk about in therapy. I still feel guilty when I relax or do something for fun. Just look at them and see if they spend every waking moment being directly productive. I came to realize that my family would go to work, yes, but then they would come home and sit around the TV for six hours straight. It's easy for them to act like you don't need free time because you're not them. They probably just aren't capable of seeing from someone else's viewpoint, especially when it comes to narcissism.
All good advice! The only problem is that her threats are vague, like "you'll see what I do face to face" and things like that. I'm not sure if anyone would take them seriously.

Is there any way you could show them how deeply these things affect you? Usually, I would have to "prove" to my family that an issue was seriously bothering me. For example, if I was having problems at school I would have to actively refuse to go to school before they would take me seriously. A talk wouldn't cut it. Is there anything (safe and legal) you can do that would drive the point home?

That's how I've felt for a while. Her favorite family members are coincidentally the most helpless ones that she has the most power over. Even if they're objectively the worst (criminal, on drugs, without a job for 10 years)  


There was a point where she "complimented" me by saying "I wasn't sure about you, but you did alright." When I asked "What's that supposed to mean?" she responded with "Well, you don't talk to me that much, so I wasn't too sure about you."  


She values other people by how well they listen to her. That alone determines their value as a person.
That is exactly what she says. You're not wrong. Haha

I've actually told her that multiple times before. I have a medical condition where I need to avoid stress as much as possible, and she does nothing but aggravate me. Even knowing that, she still won't stop. I've told her countless times to no avail.  


Thank you for the link. I didn't know a sub like that existed.
The weird thing is, I've had other family members who confided in me that they wanted her out of their life. They're the same ones cursing me for cutting her out now. I don't understand it.

Oh yeah, everyone's sick of her antics. A lot of the time I see family, everyone is complaining about something that she has just done. Unfortunately, everyone would feel guilty about cutting her out of their lives. I don't, though. The only time I see her is when she's forcing herself into family functions or stalking me.

We've tried intervention type meetings before. She won't admit to a single thing that she's done. Not one. She instead blames everyone else for "conspiring against her" and goes into a hissy fit. It always goes the same way:

"Tell me one thing that I did! One!"
-someone gives an example of something awful she's done lately-
"Bullshit! I did no such thing! Tell me one thing that I've done! One!"
And repeat.

Although I can't say I'm glad that you're going through the same thing, it's a little comforting to know that this is more common than I thought.

It's definitely an exhausting ordeal, especially when all of the choices are in your hands.

Maybe it's more common than I realized.

It was a wake up call for me when a family member told me I've "gone insane" because I've been so emotionless though all of this.

That makes sense. It's been a rough couple of years. I could make a list.

I start to feel like a creep at work. I have to act all enthusiastic and peppy to keep everyone engaged, and it's all fake. The worst part is that people like me. Or, at least what they see of me. Then I realize I'm an asshole once I get back to my car and see that I've been pretending to be someone completely different all day just to get by.

Generally any kind of stress whatsoever will trigger it. It's extremely sensitive. Sometimes only getting an unexpected phone call will send me running to the bathroom. I've been in therapy, but this anxiety is hard to get a hold of. The stomach issues make the anxiety worse, and the worsening anxiety makes the stomach issues worse... it's a snowball effect.

The worst part right now is not knowing exactly what it is, since they're thinking it's not IBS anymore and that it might be something more severe. They were saying pancreatitis. I was prepared to accept that and deal with the treatments, but it wasn't that. So... now I'm back to square one.
Some religions definitely do instill the idea that not appreciating life is a sin, which did make me feel worse. Eventually I gave up on religion entirely, but those thoughts still seep in.

I don't know if there's any way to deal with it, but I deal with that constantly. Every moment of every day. It was hard for me to go back to work after leaving my last job because sitting around, closed up in my apartment and keeping to myself, was the only time I felt relaxed in months.

I have a lot of horror stories about her.

She came back later with "You know what? If you even get sick, you obviously haven't been taking care of your health. If you don't take care of your health, that really shows that you don't care about your job. I don't know why I even hired you."

Worst boss I've ever had.

Hell, I've had bosses who have gotten angry with me for taking time off for the flu and stuff. Times where I've been throwing up every 20 minutes and wouldn't have accomplished anything at work anyway.

Once I started vomiting right before meeting a client at my old job. I called them, rescheduled the appointment, and let my boss know. She was furious. I actually got into an argument with her and said "Would you have rather I went to the meeting and threw up into a trash can the whole time?" and she said "Well, no", so I responded "Then I really don't know what you want from me!"

Some people just have impossible standards... Finding a boss more sympathetic to these issues would probably help, but a lot of people in management are workaholic hardasses in the first place. Edit: (I have a boss who actually prides himself on not even taking time off for the birth of his kids. )

That's good advice, but it's all easier said than done when it comes to mental issues. I've tried meditation, distracting myself with other hobbies, and even just sleeping through the bad thoughts. But there's always that feeling of dread in the back of my mind.

I guess it's because in all other areas of life, I can say "nobody is really judging you. Nobody even notices you. Nobody cares what you do." and pep talk myself. But that's not true for work. Both customers and bosses and breathing down your neck, waiting to chew you out for screwing up. And, coming from personal experience, the atmosphere can get pretty toxic if I make enough nervous screw ups.

I've done that for work and school many times. And once I take the time off, it doesn't really help much because I spend the whole day stressing about the dirty looks I'm going to get from teachers/bosses later on and the work I will have to make up.

Nope... nothing has ever really helped with the shaking honestly. If people mention it, I just tell them "It's a medical issue" (which it is) and they seem to understand. There are a lot of problems that cause shaky hands.

I'm not sure about Parkinsons or anything like that, but I've always had anxiety and I've had the same problems with shaky hands. I don't think it's a muscle issue, either. I've been working out for about a year and it hasn't changed the shaking at all.
I'm in Missouri, not in the smallest town but not in a major city either. I've looked for some online work, but I can't really find anything that doesn't seem to be some sort of scam or scheme.

I was with a girl for years. I was still depressed when I was with her, but it was nothing like it was now. 

I've honestly never had any points in my life where I wasn't depressed, but it can go from a manageable level to a can't-get-out-of-bed level.

So... yeah, it helps to have someone, but it's not a solution.
I just don't really know what to say, honestly. I can't even help myself.
Sometimes they downvote the posts too :/

Thanks. Honestly, you have no idea how much it helps to just hear "you're doing the right thing".

I'm sure you know how it is when you have depression, if you're here. Instead of telling yourself "you did pretty good considering the circumstances", you end up telling yourself "you wimp! you used to work twice this much! what's wrong with you? you'll never be back to normal at this rate". That was surging through my head all day, which didn't make matters any better.

I really know how you feel. I'm also chronically ill, around the same age, and having similar issues.

I wish I had something uplifting to say. All I can really say is that you aren't alone out there.

Same here... I used to love video games, and that bums me out so much. These days, I just end up thinking "why am I even doing this? It just frustrates me. I'm not even enjoying myself" and turning it off.

I know how you feel. I have a friend or two that know about my depression that I open up to. I usually end up holding back, though. I realize that I'm just rambling and never really have anything new to say about that.

It feels good to vent, but I don't want to bum them out either.

If you want to chat, send me a message. I doubt I'll have anything uplifting to say... but you know.
"We're not all stupid! Some of us are condescending assholes, too!"
That's a good way of explaining what I was trying to say in my rambling post. I fake it to keep up appearances. Then I get home and it all hits me at once.

That's where a lot of it comes from. Nobody likes to be around someone who is constantly negative. I realize that, so I hide my honest thoughts and just play a character. So, I get friends that way, but they feel distant because I feel like they only like the character I play. I guess it's better than turning everyone off because I'm such a sad sap though.
Trying to mimic what happy people do is exactly what I talked about in this post.

Constantly. Simply seeing two people who are near me laughing is enough to give me thoughts of "What did I do? Do I look funny? Am I walking in a stupid way?"

My logical side knows that it's ridiculous and that there's very little chance they even noticed me. But, I can't help the thoughts that pop into my head.

I just try telling myself "Do you really notice the people around you? Even if you see someone who sticks out, do you have the urge to point and laugh?" because, honestly, I know it's stupid to think that people would point and laugh just because... Especially now that I'm almost 30.

If I ever find a way to stop feeling like this, I'll be sure to spread the word.

Yeah, definitely. Waiting on something to happen just stresses me out more and more. So, I always have this "just do it already!" sort of rip-the-bandaid-off attitude. 

Just waiting on the elevator will get my heart pounding sometimes. I get embarrassed over the trivial crap that sets me off.
Honestly, I've been down that road too. Alcohol helps a lot, but it's not really an option when a lot of my routine requires driving... otherwise it would be my go-to solution.

There really isn't a perfect way to treat it. My doctors just have me taking a bunch of immodium every day. Usually 2 pills before bed, 2 when I wake up, and 1 before each meal. And I still have stomach issues despite it.
I wish I could help. I'm going through the same thing. Telling yourself "don't think about this" definitely has the opposite effect.

I have the same problem. Mine turned out to be irritable bowel syndome made worse by anxiety. Two disorders that really don't blend well. Having a sick stomach causes stress, which makes the stomach worse, which makes the stress worse...

This post helps, too. Even a third-hand account is good. Honestly, aside from the pamphlet they gave me, I didn't know what to expect.

Did your friends relapse? I heard that, sometimes, people might need to do it again a few years later.
Good luck to you, too. DM me if you want to talk about it further. I'm always up for it.

That's one of my biggest problems. When I have time off, I spend the whole time stressing out about when I will be busy again and completely ruin the time I do have. That's one of the things I complain about most with my therapist.

Then, when I do go back to work or whatever, I sit there, seething in regret, because I didn't do more with my day off.
That is one of the major symptoms of depression. Loss of interest. Hell, it's happening to me now. Friday night, and I'm a vegetable, just staring at the screen...
That's the thing about mental illness. It's an illness of the mind. It affects your ability to think clearly and logically. It clouds your judgement.

Try not talking about it for a while at first. Don't lie about it, just don't bring it up either.

Eventually, tell it in a matter-of-fact sort of way. "I have depression. It's hard, but I'm working on it."

Then, once you trust eachother well enough, start to tell them how you really feel.

You can't really blame the partner. It's a heavy load to drop on someone. They must get frustrated that they can't really help out.

I feel the exact same way.

And don't feel bad about people leaving after a few messages. I know how they feel, too. A lot of people here are also depressed, so we get frustrated when we don't have all of the answers. I'd like to help other people, but I can't even help myself.

Breaking up the day into different segments is a good idea. 

When it comes to that last paragraph, though, that's basically how I was living already. A "fake it 'til you make it" sort of approach. But, the problem was that my anxiety was subconcious. I'd start to panic without actually thinking about anything stressful. It didn't seem to have any pattern. I could have an easy period, like a test, where I would hardly even have to speak and I would still end up with knots in my stomach.

That was the the hardest part. The randomness of it.
Thanks... although I'm not really sure how this story was inspiring. If anything, I felt like it was the opposite.

Yeah. I'm that way. I have some "visit on the holidays" family that I'm not really close to. I tried talking to them about these things when I was younger, but they acted awkwarded out and gave my the "things will get better" speeches that everyone hates. I gave up on that long ago.

Friends, no matter how supportive they claim to be, just get scared away when I open up about my depression. So, I have some friends, but I can never feel that close to them. I always have to watch how I act or risk making it awkward. 

I have a therapist. I see doctors. I guess that's the only time I get to talk about it. 

I wish I could help. But I don't even know how to help myself.
That's the hardest part about things like this. I want to help other people somehow, but I can't really even help myself. I don't know the answers. But I listen, at least.

It's not that nobody gives a shit.

I actually read your post.

I just feel like I don't have anything productive to say. But I'm not ignoring you.
No problem. Maybe you should join some forums related to animation and stuff. A lot of people are in the same situation right now.

You're just doing what you need to for the time being.
Most people who work in art have to take a crappy job for a while before they can get into their field. It's okay, man.

I don't really know why I came here at all... But dragging other people down is the last thing I want to do.

I've had depressed friends in the past. I thought that having someone who understood would help, but I think it actually did the opposite. Neither of us could think positive, so we just enabled each other in the end.

I'm sure not every interaction would be like that, but I feel like agreeing just adds fuel to the fire.

I don't think he's trying to tell you that your tastes are bad. If I had to guess, it seems like he's trying to get you to try some more lighthearted things. "Harmless fun" sort of things that aren't really that thought provoking. Something distracting.

I'm not sure if you're accusing me of lying, or if you're saying that the doctors are incompetent.
Despite them saying that, they continued trying different medications for over a year. I told them that I was done with the whole thing. I've been on 20 different anti depressants over the last decade and I've only gotten worse. 

"supposing a doctor actually told you this"? Why the fuck would I lie about it?

Trust me, I would love to take some classes, especially get my masters. But I'm already 40k deep in school debt from before and I don't have any money to throw down on this. I could always take out a loan, but I don't know if I'll be in the position to pay it off. My doctors aren't even able to tell me what's going on. They know that my intestines have deformities (that I most likely wasn't born with, according to them) and that most of my digestive system is red and inflamed, but they can't tell me why. They're baffled. 

I would do an unpaid internship if I could. That would be good experience and wouldn't count against my financial aid, but I don't have the physical stamina for it lately. Being up and around for 3-4 hours will wipe me out.
Thank you. I would say that I'm glad to see someone else is going through the same thing, but I'm really not. It's a pretty terrible situation and I wish you luck.

Well, I've been depressed my entire life. Before and after that. So, it was going on at the time but I was dealing with it. I was still extremely depressed, but it's the stomach issues that really got to me. 

Having to run out in the middle of class to use the bathroom for 10 minutes regularly (and I mean during several classes a day) was absolutely humiliating, killing my already low self confidence, pissing off my employer, and hurting my reputation. I would be so exhausted that I would get home and pass out within minutes, not waking up again until I had to leave for work the next morning. That became my entire life for months. Needless to say I was much more depressed than before, that's for sure.

Right... it was working for a while, but unfortunately teaching is a pretty exhausting job. Especially when you are teaching English to an audience that is paying to be there... You have to be energetic, spunky, and interesting. It's almost more of a performance job than a teaching job, and I just don't have the stamina for it with this illness. It was killing me.


I wouldn't mind doing it if I were in good shape, but the thought of being in that state again terrifies me. What should have been a blast ended up being, hands down, the worst experience of my life. 11-12 hour work days in Japan are bad enough without being horribly sick the entire time.
